Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal coordination: co-term, reserved trial, auto-renew options

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We scoped next year's needs across three Atlas divisions and want to consolidate to a single renewal window if possible. A few asks from procurement and finance:

- Can we co-term the three agreements to a 2028-06-30 boundary rather than staggered dates?
- We'd like a 12-month staged ramp for reserved capacity (start 25% reserved Q1, 60% by Q4).
- Requesting an auto-renew opt-in with an annual rollback window (90 days) so we can opt-out if usage drops below threshold.
- Please provide a sample amendment, proposed pricing, and any operational notes (onboarding, canary period, service credits).

Budget is tight this year; they asked whether Redwood can offer a limited trial for the reserved buckets (30 days) before full reservation billing kicks in. If you can share a one-pager and a draft amendment, that would speed procurement.

Appreciate it — can we aim to get a draft by next Wednesday (Apr 28)?

Best,
Catherine Lin
Sr. Procurement Manager
AtlasHealth

Team — forwarding AtlasHealth's asks. Key constraints: co-term to 2028-06-30, 12-month staged reserved ramp, auto-renew with 90-day rollback, and a 30-day reserved trial.

My proposed approach (high level):
- Create a one-off amendment that:
  * Pins a co-term date of 2028-06-30 for all three divisions.
  * Adds a phased reserved capacity schedule (25% Q1, 40% Q2, 60% Q4).
  * Defines a 30-day canary trial for reserved buckets; trial billing deferred until opt-in completion.
  * Implements an annual auto-renew clause with 90-day written rollback notice; if Atlas exercises rollback, unused reserved credits convert to on-demand at a defined uplift for remaining term.
- Pricing: offer a stepped discount schedule that is conditional on reaching the staged thresholds (e.g., base reserved rate less 8% at 25%, 12% at 60%).
- SLA/credits: include a short clause for staged onboarding: two-week canary + 30-day extended acceptance window; operational playbook attached.

I've attached a draft amendment and an onboarding schedule for internal review (Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf, Onboarding_Schedule.xlsx). Please review the pricing logic and legal hooks. Jordan — can you confirm whether we can defer invoice for the 30-day trial (we typically bill from day one unless we set a trial flag). Marissa — please sanity-check the discount ladder and any commercial concessions. David — any ops risks for the staged rollout?

I want to get a clean draft to Catherine by EOD Apr 28.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf (amendment draft), Onboarding_Schedule.xlsx (ops plan)

Kim / all — quick thoughts:
- We can set a trial flag and credit Atlas for the 30-day reserved trial (defer invoicing until trial completion) but need exec sign-off on exposure cap (recommend $50k cap).
- Pricing ladder looks OK but prefer a flat uplift model on unused credits rather than converting at on-demand + arbitrary uplift. Makes legal/finance reconciliation easier.
- Co-term to 2028-06-30 is fine; we'll need to prorate the first partial period.

I'll run the numbers and post back with revenue impact. If we give a deferred-invoice trial, finance will want a short note on expected conversion rates.

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal coordination: co-term, reserved trial, auto-renew options

Adding pricing detail — rough proposal for internal review:

1) Term & Co-term
- Master amendment aligning all divisions to 2028-06-30.
- First billing period prorated to align with co-term.

2) Reserved ramp schedule (example volumes)
- Month 1-3: 25% reserved (discount: 8% off hosted unit rate)
- Month 4-6: 40% reserved (discount: 10%)
- Month 7-12: 60% reserved (discount: 14%)

3) 30-day reserved trial
- Atlas gets a 30-day trial; Redwood defers invoicing for reserved portion during trial. Exposure cap: $50,000. If Atlas cancels during trial, no reserved charges apply.

4) Auto-renew + 90-day rollback
- Annual auto-renew at the then-current rates. Atlas may opt-out within 90 days of renewal effective date via written notice. If notice received after the 90-day window, they forfeit the rollback for that year.
- If rollback is exercised, unused future reserved credits convert to on-demand at a pre-defined uplift equal to 1.25x the reserved unit rate for the balance of the term. (Jordan prefers flat uplift; we can set this at 1.15x if we want to be more competitive.)

5) Operational canary
- Two-week canary per division to validate performance; onboarding playbook governs KV cache warm-up and traffic routing.

If everyone agrees, I can fold this into Draft_Amendment_v1 and circulate.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Catherine — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a clean draft amendment (Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf) and the onboarding schedule (Onboarding_Schedule.xlsx). Key points:

- Co-term to 2028-06-30 across all three divisions; first invoice will be prorated to the new co-term boundary.
- 12-month staged reserved ramp with the discount ladder described in the amendment.
- 30-day reserved trial: Redwood will defer invoicing for the reserved portion during the trial up to a $50k exposure cap.
- Annual auto-renew with a 90-day written rollback window. If rollback is exercised, any unused reserved credits convert to on-demand at a 1.15x uplift (we chose the middle ground).
- Operational plan includes a two-week canary and a 30-day extended acceptance window.

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the draft and confirm the co-term date and exposure cap by EOD May 3.
2) If acceptable, we'll issue a DocuSign link for the amendment and set a kickoff call for the canary onboarding the week after sign.

Open to one quick call if you'd like us to walk through the amendment line by line.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
